Settings read out of the environment, through a schema, and reported all
at once.

The environment is a source like any other: a JSON body, a query string
and a database row are all read by one `Schema<A>`, and so is this. What
this module adds is the walk -- which variables a shape needs, and what to
call them -- and the report, which spells a path the way a deployment
does.

```khora
derive(Show, Decode)
type Listen = { host: String, port: Int };

derive(Show, Decode)
type Settings = { listen: Listen, password: Redacted<String>, debug: Option<Bool> };

fn settings() -> Validated<Settings, Rejection> with { env: Env } {
  read(Settings::schema())
}
```

reads `LISTEN_HOST`, `LISTEN_PORT`, `PASSWORD` and `DEBUG`, and answers
every problem rather than the first: a person fixing a deployment wants
the list, not one line of it per restart.

## How a shape becomes variable names

A field is its name in upper case; a nested record's fields are joined
to it with `_`, so `listen.port` is `LISTEN_PORT`. A list is one variable
split on commas, `TAGS=a,b`. A variant is one variable holding the case,
`MODE=Remote`, and its payload fields beside it, `MODE_URL`. A key given
by `key("http_host", ..)` replaces the field's name in that scheme and
nothing else. An optional nested record is present when any of its
variables is.

Every variable a shape needs is [`variables`], which is the question a
deployment asks and a program should not have to be started to answer.

## Why every value arrives `Untyped`

The environment cannot say whether `8080` was meant as a number, so it
does not: every value is `Raw::Untyped`, which every primitive reads.
Strictness is a fact about the source, and this source has none to offer.

## Denied is not missing

A variable the manifest does not grant is a different thing from one
nobody set, and the fix is a line in `khora.toml` rather than a line in a
deployment script. `Env::variable` raises for it; this catches the raise
into `Raw::Denied`, which decodes as `Problem::Denied`, and [`report`]
names the file.

## Functions

### read

```khora
pub fn read<A>(schema: Schema<A>) -> Validated<A, Rejection> with { env: Env }
```

Reads the settings a schema describes, every problem reported.

The schema's shape decides which variables are read and what they are
called; the schema's decoder decides what they mean. A record schema is
what this is for: a bare `int()` at the top level has no name to read.

### variables

```khora
pub fn variables(shape: Shape) -> List<String>
```

The variables a shape needs, in the order they would be read.

`[LISTEN_HOST, LISTEN_PORT, PASSWORD, DEBUG]` for the settings above.

### describe

```khora
pub fn describe(problem: Rejection) -> String
```

One line a person can act on, with the path spelled as the variable it
came from: `LISTEN_PORT should be a whole number, and is "eighty"`.

### report

```khora
pub fn report(problems: List<Rejection>) -> String
```

Every reason, one per line, in the order they were found.

What a service prints just before it stops, and the reason the whole
module answers `Validated`: this list is allowed to have more than one
thing in it.
